headword: {一攫千金|いっかくせんきん}
gloss: making a fortune at a stroke; striking it rich

definitions.gloss: making a fortune at a stroke; striking it rich; getting rich quick
definitions.explanation: Gaining a large amount of money or wealth all at once through a single opportunity. A four-character idiom (四字熟語). Literally means 'grab a thousand gold pieces in one swoop.'

examples.japanese: {一攫千金|いっかくせんきん}を{夢見|ゆめみ}る。
examples.english: To dream of striking it rich.

examples.japanese: {宝|たから}くじで{一攫千金|いっかくせんきん}を{狙|ねら}う。
examples.english: To aim for a big win with the lottery.

examples.japanese: {一攫千金|いっかくせんきん}を{狙|ねら}って{株|かぶ}に{投資|とうし}したが、{大損|おおぞん}してしまった。
examples.english: I invested in stocks hoping to strike it rich, but ended up with a huge loss.

notes:
A {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} (four-character idiom) meaning to get rich in one stroke.

ETYMOLOGY:
{一|いち} (one) + {攫|かく} (seize/grab) + {千|せん} (thousand) + {金|きん} (gold) — "grab a thousand gold pieces in one swoop."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一攫千金|いっかくせんきん}を{夢見|ゆめみ}る: to dream of striking it rich
- {一攫千金|いっかくせんきん}を{狙|ねら}う: to aim for a quick fortune
- {一攫千金|いっかくせんきん}を{手|て}にする: to get rich quick

USAGE:
Often used with a cautionary tone, implying that such get-rich-quick schemes are risky, unrealistic, or reckless. Commonly appears in contexts about gambling, lotteries, or speculative investments.
The character {攫|かく} (seize) is uncommon outside this idiom.
